optionalSupplies: Baking tray, paper and pen, one favorite solid toy (for the Indoor Harbor)
substitutes: No dark towel? Use a doormat or sheet of dark paper in the hall.
title: The Puddle Parade
clue: The rain stops. The sidewalk has turned into an archipelago.
reveal: After rain, a short loop becomes a coastline of puddle harbors. At each one your dog chooses: sail past, anchor and sniff, or wade a paw in. You only count the ports of call, and the harbor log ends in wet prints on a dark mat at the door.
objective: Walk a short loop of shallow puddles after rain, let your dog choose how to meet each one, and end with wet paw prints on the doormat.
instructions: Wait until the rain has stopped, then look out of the window: puddles on a quiet sidewalk or path near home, ankle-deep at most, with clean, clear water and a visible bottom. Choose a loop of four to six, away from traffic.
Put a dark towel or mat just inside your door: this is the harbor. Take a second towel, the leash and a water bottle. Say "Harbor Master on duty" at the door.

At the first puddle, stop a pace short and loosen the leash. Let your dog choose: Sail Past, Anchor (sniff the edge) or Wade (a paw or two in). Count each aloud as a port call, without any urging: no luring, pulling or pushing.

Never let your dog drink the puddle water. If they lap at it, step away calmly and offer your own bottle. Skip any puddle with a rainbow sheen, a smell of fuel or one that is deep or by a curb with traffic.
Keep the loop going and look for the Great Lake: the biggest safe puddle on the route. Stop there longest, offer the choice and let your dog decide how close to go.
Turn for home with the leash short. At the door, stand on the dark towel and towel-dry the paws gently, only as far as your dog likes.
Look at the dark mat before it dries: the damp paw prints are the harbor stamp. Read out the ports: how many Sail Pasts, Anchors and Wades, and where the Great Lake was.
twist: A short loop becomes a coastline of puddles, logged by your dog's choices and finished with damp paw prints on the mat.
variations: Dry Harbor for a dog who dislikes water: puddle edges only, anchor from the sidewalk and never wade. Sail Past counts as a full port call.
Doorstep Puddle for a senior or slow dog: one puddle outside the door, a sit on the step and a long anchor.

No rain today? Open the Indoor Harbor: a baking tray with one to two centimeters of fresh tap water on a towel or non-slip mat in the kitchen, bathroom or a cool, shaded balcony, with a dry towel beside it. Make a little club card with four boxes, Sniff, Paw, Splash and Lounge, and tick one for every choice your dog makes (lounging on the dry towel counts). After a few minutes, quietly set a favorite solid toy, too big to swallow, at the tray's edge or in the shallows and step back: they can take it, nose it, splash it or leave it. Never throw it in or ask for it back, then dry paws and floor and tip the tray out.
Bigger version, optional: a quiet park path after rain that you can walk to, with the same puddle rules. The loop at home is the whole adventure.
completion: You have visited at least three puddles, let your dog choose at each one and finished with the towel-dry at the door. Walking back early counts.
photoIdea: Your dog's reflection in a still puddle, taken low and from the side while they sniff the edge. No calling.
memoryPrompt: Which puddle was the Great Lake, and who was the bravest sailor?
safety: Sidewalk too hot for the back of your hand is too hot for paws, and frozen puddles hide ice: skip them in frost.
Only shallow puddles with a visible bottom, away from roads, drains and bins; skip any with a rainbow sheen.
Keep them on a leash and never let them drink puddle water; it can carry germs, oil and antifreeze.
